CI capacity: quota, LimitRange, canary, admission

section.title: Purpose
section.s: N-21 gives the factory's suite pods a namespace of their own, coq-factory, fenced so that a suite storm cannot starve the live tenants, a pod cannot read a secret, and a pod can reach only GitHub and GHCR (git, API and package ranges), cluster DNS and the Jenkins agent ports.
The ruling is D23, card C53: own factory namespace with quota, low priority, no secrets, egress to GitHub and GHCR (03-DECISIONS.md section 25).

The facts it answers: no ResourceQuota or LimitRange on any node; the Jenkins agent Role reads secrets; nine leaked kaniko-ghcr-* secrets sit in the namespace the pods run in today; Jenkins and most platform pods share ${SITE_K8S_WORKER} (L10 sections 4, 5.3 and 5.4; L07 section 3).
Input to output: a namespace.manifest record (a gitops commit) starts it; a namespace.ready record ends it; N-24 and N-26 read the newest namespace.ready before any pod is asked for.

section.title: Input record: namespace.manifest

record.s: Written by this node from the gitops mirror N-20's watch fetches ($COQ_STATE/ci/mirror/homelab-gitops.git, nodes/N-20/spec.xml#input) when the homelab-gitops main sha changes under apps/coq-factory/ or argocd-apps/workloads/coq-factory*; N-04 never fetched that repository.
record.field: sha256 over the kustomize build of apps/coq-factory at that commit (computed by the poll with kustomize build, no cluster call).
Kind and name of every object in the build, so the check knows the expected set.
sha256 of apps/coq-factory/egress-cidrs.json, the GitHub ranges the NetworkPolicy allows.

section.s: Operation key N-21/namespace.manifest/<gitops_sha>/r1.

section.title: Output record: namespace.ready

record.field: The commit the live namespace was checked against.
The revision Argo reports synced and healthy for Application coq-factory.
The live ResourceQuota hard values: pods, requests.cpu, requests.memory, limits.memory; equal to shared/ci-capacity.xml#quota.
Live defaults and maxima per container; equal to shared/ci-capacity.xml#limit-range.
name coq-pod, automount false, can_get_secrets false (from a SelfSubjectAccessReview impersonating it).
The four NetworkPolicy names present: coq-factory-default-deny, coq-factory-egress-dns, coq-factory-egress-github, coq-factory-egress-jenkins.
ExternalSecret ghcr-pull-secret status Ready and the secret's resourceVersion.
The results of shared/ci-capacity.xml#canary: dry_run (the two-container suite template admitted), dns, jenkins_agent, github_fetch, image_pull, example_blocked, duration_s.

section.s: On failure after the namespace-check layer's tries (a dry-run refusal or a failed probe at once, shared/retry-budget.xml#layers) the node writes namespace.unready (500) with the failed lines, and N-28 posts one card.

section.title: Mechanism: the manifests, the fence, the canary
section.s: The namespace is an Argo Application coq-factory (argocd-apps/workloads/coq-factory.yaml) with its own AppProject coq-factory whose destinations are namespace coq-factory only and whose clusterResourceWhitelist allows exactly PriorityClass and Namespace; the source is apps/coq-factory/ (plain kustomize, no Helm, no AVP, because nothing here holds a secret value).
section.step: Namespace coq-factory with labels pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted, pod-security.kubernetes.io/warn=restricted, and app.kubernetes.io/part-of=coq-factory; the suite pod template carries the fields restricted requires on every container, jnlp included (shared/ci-capacity.xml#pod-template), and the dry-run in step m-check proves it.

ResourceQuota coq-factory: the row and its derivation are shared/ci-capacity.xml#quota (container-cap suite pods plus one canary), rendered into apps/coq-factory/resourcequota.yaml by ci/bin/render-pod.sh (planned); this volume states no number.
LimitRange coq-factory: shared/ci-capacity.xml#limit-range, so a container that forgets resources lands at the small default and no container can exceed the case container's row.

PriorityClass coq-factory-low, value -100, globalDefault false, preemptionPolicy Never, description "factory suite pods yield to every tenant"; the pod template names it, so under pressure the scheduler starves a suite pod before a tenant pod.

ServiceAccount coq-pod with automountServiceAccountToken false and no RoleBinding of any kind; the pod template sets automountServiceAccountToken false again; Role coq-factory-pod-runner (pods, pods/exec, pods/log, pods/attach: get list watch create delete patch; events: list; no secrets, no configmaps) bound by RoleBinding to ServiceAccount jenkins:jenkins-controller (N-20 step 4) so Jenkins can run pods here and nothing else.

ExternalSecret ghcr-pull-secret in coq-factory, a copy of argocd-apps/infrastructure/jenkins-eso/externalsecret-ghcr.yaml with its own SecretStore coq-factory-ssm-store and a ServiceAccount coq-factory-eso-sa for the SSM read; the kubelet reads the secret to pull images, and no pod service account can (step 5).

Four NetworkPolicies: coq-factory-default-deny (podSelector all, policyTypes Ingress and Egress, no rules); coq-factory-egress-dns (egress to kube-dns in kube-system on UDP and TCP 53); coq-factory-egress-github (egress TCP 443 to the CIDR list in apps/coq-factory/egress-cidrs.json rendered into the policy by ci/bin/egress-policy.sh render; the list is the git, web, api and packages ranges of https://api.github.com/meta). and coq-factory-egress-jenkins (egress TCP 8080 and 50000 to namespace jenkins, pod app=jenkins), because the agent dials out to the controller; no ingress rule is needed.

ci/bin/egress-policy.sh diff reads api.github.com/meta (3 attempts, 10 s timeout each) and compares with egress-cidrs.json; on the daily tick (N-06) the Go service runs it; a difference opens a pull request on homelab-gitops with the new list as its one file (system-authored, kind mechanical), so the ranges track GitHub's changes by a merge, never by hand.

ci/bin/namespace-check.sh: after Argo reports Synced and Healthy at gitops_sha it reads every object in the expected set, compares the live quota and LimitRange with shared/ci-capacity.xml#quota and #limit-range, runs a SelfSubjectAccessReview as system:serviceaccount:coq-factory:coq-pod for get secrets (must be no), reads the ExternalSecret condition Ready, then runs every probe of shared/ci-capacity.xml#canary: the server-side dry-run of the real two-container suite template ci/pod/suite.pod.yaml as the jenkins-controller service account (quota, LimitRange and Pod Security restricted evaluated on the jnlp container too), and one canary pod from ci/pod/canary.pod.yaml with the canary row's resources that checks DNS, the Jenkins agent ports 50000 and 8080, git ls-remote of the repository, its own image pull by digest, and that https://example.com is blocked; it exits 0 only when every line holds; the pod has activeDeadlineSeconds 120 and the script deletes it on every exit.
section.mermaid: flowchart LR G[gitops commit under apps/coq-factory] --> P[N-04 writes namespace.manifest 100] P --> A{Argo Synced and Healthy at that sha within 15 min?} A -- no, 3 attempts --> U[namespace.unready 500, one card] A -- yes --> O[objects present: quota, limits, prio, SA, policies, pull secret] O --> S[can coq-pod get secrets? must be no] S --> D[dry-run of the two-container suite template] D --> C[canary pod: DNS, Jenkins 50000, git, image pull, example.com blocked] C -- both hold --> R[namespace.ready 201] C -- a line FAILED, 3 attempts --> U R --> N24[N-24 pods may run] R --> N26[N-26 full set may run]

section.title: How it starts without an agent typing
section.s: A merged gitops pull request is the only trigger; the poll (N-04) sees it on the next tick and writes namespace.manifest.

N-07 dispatches the check as a system job with a lease (key node:N-21:gitops_sha) when a namespace.manifest has no namespace.ready or namespace.unready for its sha; the same comparison runs at service start, so nothing depends on memory.

The daily tick (N-06) also dispatches a re-check against the newest gitops_sha even when a namespace.ready exists, with key node:N-21:gitops_sha:YYYYMMDD, so drift in the live cluster (a deleted quota, a hand-added RoleBinding) is found within a day and reported as namespace.unready; selfHeal in Argo repairs declared objects, and the re-check catches what Argo does not own.

section.title: Every wait, its timeout and its fallback

wait.on: Argo sync of Application coq-factory to Synced and Healthy at gitops_sha.
wait.timeout: PT15M per attempt, polled every 20 s through the kube API.
wait.fallback: The try fails as namespace-argo-not-synced (shared/retry-budget.xml#layers namespace-check); after the last try namespace.unready 500 with the Argo conditions and one card.

wait.on: ExternalSecret ghcr-pull-secret reaching condition Ready (ESO refresh 168 h, first sync within a minute).
wait.fallback: The try fails with "pull-secret: FAILED not ready" (namespace-check layer); then unready.

wait.timeout: PT3M (activeDeadlineSeconds 120 plus scheduling slack), polled every 5 s.
wait.fallback: A pod stuck Pending past PT2M counts as "canary: FAILED unschedulable" with the pod events in the log; the pod is deleted; the try fails (namespace-check layer); then unready; a 403 at the canary's create is not Pending and is unready at once (shared/ci-capacity.xml#admission).
The diff is skipped for the day and a counter increments; the policy keeps yesterday's list; after 7 skipped days an alert (N-41) fires.

section.s: The check job's stall bound is PT30M, enforced by N-12; a stalled check is killed, its lease revoked and the attempt counted.

section.title: Retries, recovery and the report
section.s: Every kube API call is retried by the namespace-call layer (backoff 2 s, 4 s, 8 s) before it is a failed line; the check is retried by the namespace-check layer with N-11's backoff (shared/retry-budget.xml#layers, each failure class by one layer only); a dry-run refusal, a probe that fails, a quota or LimitRange that differs from shared/ci-capacity.xml is a result and writes namespace.unready 500 at once; one card, deduped on node:N-21:gitops_sha.

The canary pod is deleted on every exit path of the script, including a kill: the script traps EXIT and the pod carries activeDeadlineSeconds, so a dead check leaves at most one pod that ends itself within two minutes; the daily cleanup (section state-paths) reaps any leftover.
A namespace.unready is terminal for its sha; a newer gitops commit or a ruling re-enters at N-03.

section.title: Many agents at once
section.s: Readers: N-24 asks for pods and N-26 asks for a full run only after reading the newest namespace.ready; the record is immutable and keyed by sha, so N readers agree on the same precondition.

Pods at once: the quota, the LimitRange and the Jenkins containerCap bound how many suite pods exist whatever the number of gate runs (shared/ci-capacity.xml#model); the cap and the in-flight rule equal the quota's suite share, so the quota is never hit in normal operation; a pod refused by the quota is a 403 at create, never a Pending pod, and N-24 records it as admission-refused, a capacity.defect and one card without climbing (shared/ci-capacity.xml#admission).
Two checks on two gitops shas: the newer wins; the older's lease is revoked with 410 by N-07; two Go service instances cannot both hold the lease (fencing token, 412 stale_token on the stale write).

Two canaries: the canary pod name carries the gitops sha12 and the attempt, so two checks never share a pod; the quota reserves room for one canary beside the full container cap, and the lease per sha makes a second concurrent canary impossible except across two shas, where the older check is revoked first.
Hand edits in the cluster by anyone: Argo selfHeal reverts declared objects within its poll; undeclared additions are found by the daily re-check and reported, never silently kept.
Collision answer in one line: one lease per sha, immutable records, quota as the physical bound, newest sha wins, drift reported daily.

section.title: Status codes this node emits
section.emits: Nobody acts; N-07 dispatches the check.
N-24 and N-26 read it as their precondition.
Nobody acts; a newer gitops sha replaced this check.
N-28 posts one card; N-24 and N-26 write 423 until a newer namespace.ready exists.
Written by N-24 or N-26 when no namespace.ready 201 exists; one card per cause.

section.title: State paths and the cleanup script for each
section.path: One log per attempt with every assertion line and the canary output.

path.p: cluster: namespace coq-factory, pods named coq-canary-*

section.path: Deletes finished or stuck pods older than the age in coq-factory; dry-run lists them.
Only for retiring the factory: deletes the Argo Application with the resources finalizer first, then the namespace, in that order (L10 section 8 item 8); refuses while any gate.run is in flight.

section.path: The source of truth; not state.
section.s: Every script prints its plan without --apply, acts only with --apply, retries each deletion 3 times and exits 4 listing what remains; N-45 registers them.

section.title: DAG edges in and out
section.in: namespace.manifest is written by the GitHub poll of homelab-gitops; the DAG draws no edge into N-21 because the input is a commit.
section.out: namespace.ready is the precondition of every suite pod.
namespace.ready is the precondition of the full-set run on main.

section.title: Permissions
section.s: The Go service: kubeconfig for ServiceAccount coq-reconciler with get and list on applications in argocd, get and list on resourcequotas, limitranges, serviceaccounts, rolebindings, networkpolicies, externalsecrets in coq-factory, get on priorityclasses, create and delete on pods in coq-factory limited by a resourceNames-free Role but with the LimitRange as the ceiling, create on selfsubjectaccessreviews and subjectaccessreviews; credential kubeconfig (shared/authority.xml#credential-matrix); the gitops mirror is N-20's; the CIDR bump pull request on homelab-gitops needs a gitops pull-request credential that the matrix does not yet carry (named in the 1.1.0 report), and until it exists the diff writes one card instead.
Jenkins controller: pods, pods/exec, pods/log in coq-factory only (step 5); no secrets anywhere once N-20 removes cluster-admin.
Suite pods: service account coq-pod with no token mounted; egress to GitHub ranges, DNS and the Jenkins service; nothing else.
Seats: may edit apps/coq-factory/ only inside a ticket declaring those files; no kube access of any kind.
The owner: kubectl as ${SITE_K8S_ADMIN} for break glass; a change is reverted by selfHeal or reported by the daily re-check.

section.title: Monitoring
section.s: Status call fields for N-21: newest namespace.ready sha and age, quota used versus hard (pods, cpu, memory) read on every scheduler tick, canary duration p95, egress diff skipped days.
Alerts (N-41): namespace.unready; quota used at 100 percent for more than PT10M (a stuck pod); egress diff skipped 7 days; Pod Security violation events in coq-factory (an image or template drift).
Map (N-38): the N-21 machine lamp green on 201, red on unready; the stats screen shows pods in coq-factory as a belt throughput counter.

section.title: Runbook
section.step: First bring-up: the gitops pull request adds apps/coq-factory and the Application; after merge, nothing else is typed; the Go service's poll and check produce namespace.ready; the proof is the record.

GitHub range change: the daily diff opens the pull request; a reviewer seat is not needed for a system-authored one-file change (shared seat-contract clause mechanical-pr); the machine merge (N-09) lands it on green.

Measured contention (tenant pod evictions or latency alerts while suites run): lower the quota in gitops first; only if that fails cut a ticket for D23 option C, a tainted node, which the owner rules.

Cleanup: ci/bin/cleanup-cluster.sh --what factory-pods --older-than 2h; ci/bin/cleanup-ci-state.sh --what namespace-check --older-than 30d; ci/bin/cleanup-cluster.sh --what factory-namespace to retire (refuses while a gate.run is in flight).
Retiring the namespace: Application with finalizer first, AppProject in a later commit, namespace last (L10 section 8 item 8 lessons).

rejected.source: 03-DECISIONS.md D23 option A, share namespace jenkins
rejected.reason: Pods keep a path to secrets and no quota bounds them; ruled out by C53.

rejected.source: 03-DECISIONS.md D23 option C, a tainted Pi for the factory
rejected.reason: Loses two thirds of the cluster for slow serial suites; kept as runbook R3 only after measured contention.

rejected.source: DNS-name egress policy (allow github.com by name)
rejected.reason: Calico open source has no domain selector; that needs Calico Enterprise or Cilium, a cluster change outside this rebuild; CIDRs from api.github.com/meta tracked by a daily diff do the job.

rejected.source: S02 Kueue for queueing and reserved slots
rejected.reason: Kueue's supported range starts above this cluster's 1.32 and a fixed slot count already does the job (S02 section 8).

rejected.source: Per-build secrets created inside a build (jenkins-shared-lib buildKaniko.groovy:53)
rejected.reason: Leaks on abort (nine leaked); the namespace has one ESO-synced pull secret and no build may create a secret here (the runner Role has no secrets verb).

rejected.source: Pod Security baseline instead of restricted
rejected.reason: The pod template already runs non-root with no privileges; restricted costs three fields and closes escalation by construction.
